we have proposed a novel algorithm for the detection of granules in electron microscopy images and a new methodology to statistically analyze their spatial distribution in different cell groups.
the spatial distribution of granules can be characterized by functional descriptors, and that the descriptors and the testing procedures allow discriminating between different cell groups.
we have developed a method that automatically detects granules in cells and allows the statistical analysis of the spatial distribution of granules in cells.

the development of novel tools for the analysis of the spatial distribution of granules in the cell cytoplasma, which should help in the study of diseases related to dysfunctional secretion, as diabetes.
the development of novel tools for the analysis of spatial point processes in the context of replicated point patterns.
the statistical analysis of replicated point patterns and the application of this analysis to the characterization of granule locations in different cell types.

the method presented in the paper is a powerful tool for the analysis of the spatial distribution of secretory granules.
the proposed methodology provides a useful framework for the study of the intracellular organization of granules in secretory cells.
the proposed descriptors are useful to detect differences in granule distribution between groups of secretory cells.

the proposed statistical tools are suitable for analyzing replicated point patterns of granules in different groups of cells and that the analysis of these point patterns can provide useful information for the understanding of the secretory process.
